data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 'Recovery Signature' (temporal alignment of restoration) is the primary evidence distinguishing truly independent failures from those with a hidden shared cause.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The recovery process is triggered by a global automated health-check system that restarts all services simultaneously.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The services are logically independent but physically co-located on the same hardware/hypervisor.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independent failures occur and resolve according to the local state of individual services; however, if a cluster of seemingly unrelated services all recover within a narrow, synchronized time window, it indicates a shared external trigger (e.g., a BGP route leak or global API outage) that was the actual source of the correlation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
